liner.body_md:
## What listeners single out

- **Dark Star** (3 reviews): Dark Star features layered, unique jamming from about the 19-minute point to the end, despite a cut; About ten minutes of alien sounds and near silence open the jam between verses, then it becomes a very hot jam [6][13][14]
- **Turn On Your Lovelight** (3 reviews): Lovelight provides a perfect rave-up ending to the set; Lovelight is said to rage, even more than The Eleven [6][15][16]
- **Mason's Children** (1 review): The Mason's Children here matches the version on the Fallout from the Phil Zone release and is brilliant [5]
- **The Other One** (1 review): The Other One goes out far and really travels [14]
- **Cryptical Envelopment** (1 review): Reviewer loves the segue from Cryptical Envelopment into Cosmic Charlie [8]
- **High Time** (1 review): High Time is very well executed, the reviewer's probable favorite version by the band [14]
- **St. Stephen** (1 review): St. Stephen following Dark Star is called the funkiest ever, with a great funky sound [13]
- **The Eleven** (1 review): The Eleven is described as one of the all-time powerhouse versions [6]

## The recordings

- **gd70-01-02.early-late.sbd.cotsman.18120.sbeok.shnf** (recommended): matrix (soundboard mixed with audience mics); 24 songs; 182 min; rated 4.21/5 by 46 [1]
- **gd70-01-02.late.sbd.hanno.12624.sbefail.shnf**: soundboard; 13 songs; 71 min; rated 2.67/5 by 6 [3]
- **gd70-01-02.partial-early.sbd.86.sbefail.shnf**: soundboard; 4 songs; 35 min; rated 4.5/5 by 22 [4]. Said about its sound: Cymbals, maracas and snare sit right up front in the recording; Dark Star sounds especially good on good speakers; Tape hiss is present and unavoidable, but the Dark Star is treated delicately; best heard with lights out; There is a cut at the end of Dark Star and start of St. Stephen [4][7][12]
- **gd1970-01-02.137375.sbd.wise.sirmick.sbeok.flac16**: soundboard; 25 songs; 180 min; rated 3.33/5 by 9 [2]

## Around the show

- Stage talk about: Zarathustra [1]
- Reviewer says deadlists.com lists this as the Early show, though the file is labeled Late [8]
- Set was relabeled Early in 2001 on a witness account, but deadlists.com later found more evidence for Late [2]
- The Dark Star is one of the last with Tom Constanten, who adds a section resembling Seastones [8]
- The Dark Star is ranked among the best of 1970, with superb post-verse jamming and an eye-opening spacey portion [15]

## Tapers and lineage

- **gd70-01-02.early-late.sbd.cotsman.18120.sbeok.shnf**: source: Soundboard [1]. Also: Matrix of early and late shows, credited to A. Lemiex, Uli and Hanno [1]
- **gd70-01-02.late.sbd.hanno.12624.sbefail.shnf**: source: Soundboard [3]. Also: Soundboard with audience patches, passed along via Hanno Bunjes and Uli Teute; labeled late show [3]
- **gd70-01-02.partial-early.sbd.86.sbefail.shnf**: transferred by Stephen Windsor; source: Soundboard [4]. Also: Partial soundboard transferred via master reel to DAT, then CDR and EAC; from S. Windsor, D. Sacks to etree [4]
- **gd1970-01-02.137375.sbd.wise.sirmick.sbeok.flac16**: taped by Jim Wise; transferred by SIRMick; source: Soundboard > 7 1/2' Reel Master @ 7.5 ips (Recorded By Bear on a Sony 770 Reel Deck) > 1st gen (TDK SAX-100 cassette) from Dick Latvala (Master Reel Playback… [2]
